skills.title: Kubernetes Basics
skills.description: Deploy applications to Kubernetes with deployments and services.
skills.content:
# Kubernetes Basics

I help you deploy applications to Kubernetes.

## Deployment
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: my-app:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 3000
          env:
            - name: NODE_ENV
              value: production
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: "128Mi"
              cpu: "100m"
            limits:
              memory: "256Mi"
              cpu: "500m"
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 3000
```

## Service
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  selector:
    app: my-app
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 3000
  type: ClusterIP
```

## Ingress
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  rules:
    - host: app.example.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: my-app
                port:
                  number: 80
```

# Docker Containerization

I help you containerize applications with Docker.

## Node.js Dockerfile
```dockerfile
# Build stage
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

# Production stage
FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder /app/package.json ./

USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]
```

## Docker Compose
```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  app:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@db:5432/app
    depends_on:
      - db
      - redis

  db:
    image: postgres:15-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: user
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: pass
      POSTGRES_DB: app
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine

volumes:
  postgres_data:
```

## Best Practices
- Use multi-stage builds
- Run as non-root user
- Use specific image tags
- Add .dockerignore file
- Cache dependencies layer

skills.content:
# GitHub Actions CI/CD

I help you build CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions.

## Basic Workflow
```yaml
name: CI/CD
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test

  deploy:
    needs: test
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Deploy
        run: ./deploy.sh
        env:
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
```

## Matrix Testing
```yaml
strategy:
  matrix:
    node: [18, 20, 22]
    os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
steps:
  - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    with:
      node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
```

## Reusable Workflows
```yaml
# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      environment:
        required: true
        type: string
```

# Monorepo Management

I help you manage monorepos effectively.

## Turborepo Setup
```json
// turbo.json
{
  "$schema": "https://turbo.build/schema.json",
  "pipeline": {
    "build": {
      "dependsOn": ["^build"],
      "outputs": ["dist/**", ".next/**"]
    },
    "test": {
      "dependsOn": ["build"]
    },
    "lint": {},
    "dev": {
      "cache": false,
      "persistent": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Workspace Structure
```
monorepo/
├── apps/
│   ├── web/          # Next.js frontend
│   ├── api/          # NestJS backend
│   └── mobile/       # React Native app
├── packages/
│   ├── ui/           # Shared components
│   ├── config/       # Shared configs
│   └── types/        # Shared TypeScript types
├── turbo.json
└── package.json
```

## Shared Dependencies
```json
// Root package.json
{
  "workspaces": ["apps/*", "packages/*"],
  "devDependencies": {
    "turbo": "latest",
    "typescript": "^5.0.0"
  }
}
```

## Commands
```bash
turbo build           # Build all packages
turbo dev --filter=web  # Run specific app
turbo lint --affected   # Only changed packages
```

skills.description: Process and analyze text with NLP techniques and transformers.
skills.content:
# Natural Language Processing

I help you process and analyze text data.

## Text Preprocessing
```python
import re
import nltk
from nltk.corpus import stopwords
from nltk.stem import WordNetLemmatizer

nltk.download(['stopwords', 'wordnet', 'punkt'])

def preprocess_text(text: str) -> str:
    # Lowercase
    text = text.lower()
    # Remove special characters
    text = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z\s]', '', text)
    # Tokenize
    tokens = nltk.word_tokenize(text)
    # Remove stopwords
    stop_words = set(stopwords.words('english'))
    tokens = [t for t in tokens if t not in stop_words]
    # Lemmatize
    lemmatizer = WordNetLemmatizer()
    tokens = [lemmatizer.lemmatize(t) for t in tokens]
    return ' '.join(tokens)
```

## Sentiment Analysis
```python
from transformers import pipeline

sentiment = pipeline("sentiment-analysis")
result = sentiment("I love this product!")
# [{'label': 'POSITIVE', 'score': 0.9998}]
```

## Text Classification
```python
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.naive_bayes import MultinomialNB

# Vectorize text
vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer(max_features=5000)
X_train_tfidf = vectorizer.fit_transform(X_train)

# Train classifier
clf = MultinomialNB()
clf.fit(X_train_tfidf, y_train)

# Predict

skills.title: Data Pipeline Design
skills.description: Build reliable ETL data pipelines with validation and scheduling.
skills.content:
# Data Pipeline Design

I help you build reliable data pipelines.

## ETL with Python
```python
from datetime import datetime
import pandas as pd

def extract(source: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Extract data from source."""
    return pd.read_csv(source)

def transform(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Clean and transform data."""
    df = df.dropna()
    df['amount'] = df['amount'].astype(float)
    df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
    df['year_month'] = df['date'].dt.to_period('M')
    return df

def load(df: pd.DataFrame, destination: str) -> None:
    """Load data to destination."""
    df.to_parquet(destination, index=False)

def run_pipeline():
    """Run the full ETL pipeline."""
    raw = extract('data/raw.csv')
    cleaned = transform(raw)
    load(cleaned, 'data/processed.parquet')
    print(f"Pipeline completed: {len(cleaned)} rows processed")
```

## Scheduling
```python
# Using APScheduler
from apscheduler.schedulers.blocking import BlockingScheduler

scheduler = BlockingScheduler()

@scheduler.scheduled_job('cron', hour=6)
def daily_job():
    run_pipeline()

scheduler.start()
```

## Data Validation
```python
import pandera as pa

schema = pa.DataFrameSchema({
    "id": pa.Column(int, unique=True),
    "amount": pa.Column(float, pa.Check.greater_than(0)),
    "email": pa.Column(str, pa.Check.str_matches(r'^[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.\w+$')),
})

validated_df = schema.validate(df)
```

skills.title: A/B Testing Framework
skills.description: Design and analyze A/B tests with proper statistical methods.
skills.content:
# A/B Testing Framework

I help you design and analyze A/B tests.

## Sample Size Calculation
```python
from statsmodels.stats.power import TTestIndPower

# Calculate required sample size
power_analysis = TTestIndPower()
sample_size = power_analysis.solve_power(
    effect_size=0.2,  # Minimum detectable effect
    alpha=0.05,       # Significance level
    power=0.8,        # Statistical power
    alternative='two-sided'
)
print(f"Required sample size per group: {int(sample_size)}")
```

## Conversion Rate Test
```python
from scipy.stats import chi2_contingency

# Contingency table
#              Converted  Not Converted
# Control         50          450
# Treatment       70          430

observed = [[50, 450], [70, 430]]
chi2, p_value, dof, expected = chi2_contingency(observed)

# Conversion rates
control_rate = 50 / 500
treatment_rate = 70 / 500
lift = (treatment_rate - control_rate) / control_rate
print(f"Lift: {lift:.1%}")
```

## Continuous Metrics (T-Test)
```python
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

# Compare means
t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(control_values, treatment_values)

# Effect size (Cohen's d)
def cohens_d(group1, group2):
    n1, n2 = len(group1), len(group2)
    var1, var2 = group1.var(), group2.var()
    pooled_std = np.sqrt(((n1-1)*var1 + (n2-1)*var2) / (n1+n2-2))
    return (group1.mean() - group2.mean()) / pooled_std
```

skills.description: Analyze and forecast time series data with decomposition and ARIMA.
skills.content:
# Time Series Analysis

I help you analyze and forecast time series data.

## Time Series Basics
```python
import pandas as pd

# Create time series
df['date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'])
df = df.set_index('date')
df = df.sort_index()

# Resample
df.resample('D').sum()  # Daily
df.resample('W').mean()  # Weekly
df.resample('M').sum()  # Monthly
```

## Trend and Seasonality
```python
from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import seasonal_decompose

# Decomposition
result = seasonal_decompose(df['value'], model='additive', period=12)
result.plot()

# Access components
trend = result.trend
seasonal = result.seasonal
residual = result.resid
```

## Simple Forecasting
```python
from statsmodels.tsa.holtwinters import ExponentialSmoothing

# Holt-Winters
model = ExponentialSmoothing(
    df['value'],
    seasonal_periods=12,
    trend='add',
    seasonal='add'
)
fitted = model.fit()
forecast = fitted.forecast(12)
```

## ARIMA Model
```python
from statsmodels.tsa.arima.model import ARIMA

model = ARIMA(df['value'], order=(1, 1, 1))
fitted = model.fit()
forecast = fitted.forecast(steps=12)
```

skills.title: SQL Analytics Queries
skills.description: Write analytical SQL with window functions, CTEs, and cohort analysis.
skills.content:
# SQL Analytics Queries

I help you write analytical SQL queries.

## Window Functions
```sql
-- Running total
SELECT
  date,
  amount,
  SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY date) as running_total
FROM orders;

-- Rank within group
SELECT
  name,
  department,
  salary,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) as dept_rank
FROM employees;

-- Moving average
SELECT
  date,
  value,
  AVG(value) OVER (
    ORDER BY date
    ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) as moving_avg_7d
FROM metrics;
```

## CTEs for Readability
```sql
WITH monthly_sales AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', created_at) as month,
    SUM(amount) as total
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY 1
),
growth AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    total,
    LAG(total) OVER (ORDER BY month) as prev_month,
    total - LAG(total) OVER (ORDER BY month) as growth
  FROM monthly_sales
)
SELECT * FROM growth;
```

## Cohort Analysis
```sql
WITH cohorts AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', MIN(created_at)) as cohort_month
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  cohort_month,
  DATE_TRUNC('month', o.created_at) as order_month,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id) as users
FROM orders o
JOIN cohorts c ON o.user_id = c.user_id
GROUP BY 1, 2;
```

skills.content:
# Database Connection Pool Manager

I optimize database connection management.

## Connection Pooling Basics

### Why Pool?
- Creating connections is expensive
- Limits protect database from overload
- Reuse improves performance

### Configuration
```typescript
const pool = new Pool({
  max: 20,              // Maximum connections
  min: 5,               // Minimum connections
  idleTimeoutMillis: 30000,
  connectionTimeoutMillis: 5000,
});
```

## Sizing Guidelines

| Connections Formula |
|---------------------|
| connections = (cores * 2) + spindle_disks |
| For SSD: connections = cores * 2 |

### Per-Application Limits
- API servers: 10-20 per instance
- Background workers: 5-10 per worker
- Total < PostgreSQL max_connections

## Best Practices

### Release Connections
```typescript
// Always release back to pool
const client = await pool.connect();
try {
  await client.query('SELECT...');
} finally {
  client.release();
}
```

### Monitor Pool Health
- Check waiting connections
- Monitor connection age
- Alert on pool exhaustion

# Database Migration Expert

I help you manage database migrations safely.

## Migration Workflow

### Generate Migration
```bash
npm run db:generate
```

### Review Generated SQL
Always review before running:
- Check for destructive changes
- Verify index creation
- Ensure rollback is possible

### Run Migration
```bash
npm run db:migrate
```

## Safe Migration Practices

### Adding Columns
```sql
-- Safe: nullable or with default
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN bio TEXT;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN status TEXT DEFAULT 'active';
```

### Renaming Columns (Multi-step)
1. Add new column
2. Backfill data
3. Update application code
4. Drop old column (later migration)

### Adding NOT NULL
```sql
-- 1. Add column nullable
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN role TEXT;
-- 2. Backfill data
UPDATE users SET role = 'user' WHERE role IS NULL;
-- 3. Add constraint
ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN role SET NOT NULL;
```

## Rollback Strategy
Always test rollbacks in staging before production.

```sql

SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = 123;

CREATE INDEX idx_orders_user_id ON orders(user_id);
-- Now: Index Scan (fast)

```sql

SELECT * FROM users;

-- ✅ Good
SELECT id, email, name FROM users;
```

### N+1 Query Problem
```sql
-- ❌ Bad: N+1 queries
for each user:
  SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = ?

-- ✅ Good: Single query
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id IN (1, 2, 3...);

SELECT * FROM posts
WHERE created_at < $cursor

### When to Normalize (3NF)
- Transactional data (orders, payments)
- Frequently updated data
- Data integrity is critical

### When to Denormalize
- Read-heavy workloads
- Reporting/analytics
- Known query patterns

## PostgreSQL Best Practices

### Primary Keys
```sql
-- UUID for distributed systems
id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()

-- Serial for simple apps
id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY
```

### Indexes
```sql
-- Composite index for common queries
CREATE INDEX idx_users_status_created
  ON users(status, created_at DESC);

-- Partial index for filtered queries
CREATE INDEX idx_active_users
  ON users(email) WHERE status = 'active';
```

### Foreign Keys
```sql
user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
```

## Common Patterns
- Soft deletes with `deleted_at` timestamp
- Audit columns: `created_at`, `updated_at`
- JSONB for flexible metadata

# Git History Surgeon

I help you craft clean Git history through safe rewriting operations.

## Interactive Rebase

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~N
```

### Rebase Commands
| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `pick` | Keep commit as-is |
| `reword` | Edit commit message |
| `edit` | Stop to amend commit |
| `squash` | Meld into previous commit |
| `fixup` | Squash, discard message |
| `drop` | Remove commit |

## Common Operations

### Squash Last N Commits
```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~N
git commit -m "Combined commit message"
```

### Amend Last Commit
```bash
git commit --amend -m "New message"
```

### Split a Commit
```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~N  # Mark as 'edit'
git reset HEAD^
git add -p            # Stage selectively
git commit -m "First part"
```

## Safety Rules
1. Never rewrite published history
2. Always backup first: `git branch backup`
3. Use `--force-with-lease` instead of `--force`

## Supported Strategies

### Git Flow
Best for: Scheduled releases, multiple version support

```
main ─────────────────────────────────►
       ↑                    ↑
release/1.0 ──────► merge   │
       ↑                    │
develop ──────────────────────────────►
       ↑         ↑
feature/login ──► merge
```

**Branches:**
- `main` - Production-ready code only
- `develop` - Integration branch for features
- `feature/*` - Individual feature development
- `release/*` - Release preparation
- `hotfix/*` - Emergency production fixes

### Trunk-Based Development
Best for: Continuous deployment, experienced teams
- All developers commit to main
- Short-lived feature branches (< 2 days)
- Feature flags for incomplete work

### GitHub Flow
Best for: Web applications, continuous delivery
1. Create branch from main
2. Add commits
3. Open Pull Request
4. Review and discuss
5. Merge to main

skills.content:
# API Designer

I design clean, consistent, and well-documented REST APIs.

## Resource Naming
```
GET    /users              # List users
POST   /users              # Create user
GET    /users/:id          # Get user
PUT    /users/:id          # Replace user
PATCH  /users/:id          # Update user
DELETE /users/:id          # Delete user
GET    /users/:id/posts    # User's posts
```

## HTTP Status Codes
| Code | Use Case |
|------|----------|
| 200 | Success |
| 201 | Created |
| 204 | No Content (delete) |
| 400 | Bad Request |
| 401 | Unauthorized |
| 403 | Forbidden |
| 404 | Not Found |
| 422 | Validation Error |

## Best Practices
- Use nouns for resources, not verbs
- Consistent response formats
- Pagination for lists
- Versioning strategy (URL or header)
- OpenAPI/Swagger documentation

skills.title: Debugging Assistant
skills.description: Systematic debugging skill that helps identify, analyze, and fix bugs in code.
skills.content:
# Debugging Assistant

I help you systematically identify, analyze, and fix bugs in your code.

## Debugging Process

### 1. Reproduce
- Understand exact steps to reproduce
- Identify consistent vs intermittent issues
- Document expected vs actual behavior

### 2. Isolate
- Narrow down to specific code sections
- Use binary search to find the problem
- Create minimal reproduction case

### 3. Analyze
- Examine error messages and stack traces
- Check logs for context
- Verify assumptions about data

### 4. Hypothesize
- Form theories about root causes
- Consider recent changes
- Check for common patterns

### 5. Fix & Verify
- Implement targeted fix
- Add tests to prevent regression
- Verify in all affected scenarios

I explain reasoning so you learn debugging techniques.

skills.content:
# Code Review Expert

I conduct thorough code reviews focusing on correctness, security, performance, and best practices.

## Review Checklist

### Correctness
- Logic handles edge cases
- Error handling is appropriate
- Types are correctly defined
- Business requirements are met

### Security
- Input validation present
- No hardcoded secrets
- SQL injection prevented
- XSS vulnerabilities addressed

### Performance
- No N+1 query problems
- Appropriate data structures used
- Expensive operations cached or optimized

### Maintainability
- Code is readable and self-documenting
- Functions are appropriately sized
- DRY principle followed
- Consistent naming conventions

Provide specific, actionable feedback with code examples when suggesting improvements.
